source: Wang H. (2024) A Content-Based Novelty Measure for Scholarly Publications: A Proof of Concept
finding: Treats novelty as atypical combination at the word level. Novelty score is the average surprisal of a paper's tokens under a small GPT-2 trained only on Wikipedia. No citation data needed.
numbers: GPT-2 124M params, trained on 6.5M Wikipedia docs (4.6B tokens). Face validity: 'room' (4.42 bits) vs 'low' (2.58 bits) temperature token; 20 ChatGPT paraphrases per sentence, Welch t=2.9, p=0.003, df~36.5.
quote: novelty as the atypical combination of existing knowledge
limits: Proof of concept. Wikipedia is a weak stand-in for scholarly discourse. Style, maths notation and a research group's consistent voice move the score.
agent_relevance: A cheap, token-level 'how surprising is this to a reference model' signal that an agent can compute on its own candidate thoughts without any citation graph.

source: Wang H. (2024) A Content-Based Novelty Measure for Scholarly Publications: A Proof of Concept (construct validity)
finding: Known-groups test on 80 usable PAN authorship-verification working notes (83 collected, 3 too short). Papers that all three experts called novel had higher mean surprisal.
numbers: 25 of 80 papers in the novel group (unanimous by 3 experts). One-tailed Welch t=2.6, p=0.005, df~66.3. Eight 'false alarms' above 5.0 bits judged not novel: 2 heavy maths, 1 informal 'you' syntax, 3 incremental papers from one team, 2 marginal.
limits: One narrow venue and task, binary expert labels, conservative unanimity rule. Effect size not reported. Surprisal confounds novelty with odd style.
agent_relevance: Shows a surprisal score separates 'novel' from 'normal' only on average. An agent should use it as a weak ranking cue, and should strip style and notation before scoring.

source: Safari & Babaei (2026) Research Novelty in Information Systems Journals After ChatGPT
finding: Uses SPECTER2 embedding distance from the nearest recent papers as abstract-level semantic novelty. After 2022, articles with first authors in non-English-dominant countries lost more relative novelty than English-dominant ones.
numbers: 13,847 articles, 2020-2025, 44 A*/A IS journals. Post x Non-EDA coefficient -0.176 SD (p<0.001), about 7 percentile points. Balanced repeat-author panel same direction but imprecise.
limits: No measure of actual LLM use, so it is a post-2022 shift, not a causal LLM effect. Affiliation country is a crude proxy. Measures title and abstract wording only.
agent_relevance: Warns that an embedding-distance novelty score also moves with wording and framing, not only ideas. Any agent novelty check on text must separate framing from content.

source: Safari & Babaei (2026) Research Novelty in IS Journals After ChatGPT (framing of prior work)
finding: Paper summarises two competing paths for AI in knowledge work: knowledge expansion (new combinations) and standardisation (familiar frames reproduced). Cites Liu et al. 2025: over 32 million papers to 2019, papers with more AI terms had higher novelty and disruption.
numbers: Liu et al. 2025: >32M papers through 2019 (as reported here). Kwon and Yang 2025: >218,000 CS papers, output rose after ChatGPT (as reported here).
limits: Second-hand report of Liu et al. 2025 and Kwon and Yang 2025; those originals were not opened.
agent_relevance: The same tool can raise recombination range and also pull outputs to the common centre. A scaffold needs a step that pushes away from the centre, not just widens the search.

source: Liu Y., Yang Z., Poria S., Nguyen T., Cambria E. (2025) Harnessing Large Language Models for Scientific Novelty Detection
finding: Builds two closure-set datasets (Marketing, NLP). Distils LLM idea-level similarity into a small retriever, then asks an LLM to score the target idea against each retrieved idea on a 5-level rubric; a decision tree turns the scores into novel / not novel.
numbers: Marketing: 470 seed papers, 12,577 papers. NLP: 3,533 seeds, 32,239 papers. Retrieval gain over best baseline +5.40% (Marketing) and +15.19% (NLP). Test sets 100 samples each, 1:1 balanced.
limits: Non-novel negatives are synthetic (GPT-4o-mini rephrased, partial, incremental ideas), so this tests duplicate detection more than true novelty. Small test sets.
agent_relevance: Retrieve-then-compare is the working pattern: find nearest prior ideas first, score against each, then decide. Plain text similarity misses paraphrases.

source: Liu Y. et al. (2025) Harnessing LLMs for Scientific Novelty Detection (baseline comparison incl. Uzzi-style)
finding: The classic Uzzi-style unusual journal-pair score (URPC) is near chance as a binary novelty detector on these sets. The RAG + distilled retriever method beats all baselines.
numbers: Accuracy Marketing / NLP: URPC 0.5500 / 0.4800; CD (cited-reference embeddings) 0.6005 / 0.5167; PES 0.47 / 0.58; MOOSE (direct LLM judge) 0.6400 / 0.5900; SciMON 0.49 / 0.61; RAG-Vanilla 0.7292 / 0.6100; RAG-KD 0.7453 / 0.7474 (F1 0.7344 / 0.7349). Best LLM backbone: deepseek-reasoner over gpt-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B.
limits: Baselines were applied to idea text, a task they were not built for. URPC needs reference lists, so the comparison is partly unfair. Only 100 test items.
agent_relevance: Citation-pair atypicality does not work on bare ideas; an LLM with retrieved comparators does. Choose the comparator-retrieval design for an in-loop novelty check.

source: Liu Y. et al. (2025) Harnessing LLMs for Scientific Novelty Detection (K and rubric)
finding: Prompt gives a 5-level rubric from 0.0 to 1.0 (no, low, moderate, high, very high novelty) based on how much of the idea overlaps an existing idea. A moderate number of retrieved ideas works best; too many hurts.
numbers: Best K about 5 to 10; K=20 not better. Rubric anchors: 0.3 subset of existing idea, 0.5 about 50% overlap, 0.7 small overlap, 1.0 distinct direction.
limits: Figure-level result for K; exact scores not read from table. Authors suggest the long-context limit of LLMs as the cause.
agent_relevance: Compare to a handful of nearest items, not a long list. A graded overlap rubric is a ready prompt for a novelty check step.

source: Schopf T. & Faerber M. (2026) Is this Idea Novel? An Automated Benchmark for Judgment of Research Ideas (RINoBench)
finding: Seven LLMs judge novelty of ICLR ideas on a 1-5 rubric given related works. Their written reasons match human reasons closely, but their scores are poor.
numbers: 1,381 ideas (ICLR 2022 and 2023). Macro F1: GPT-5 17.2, o3 16.2, DeepSeek-R1 14.6, Llama-3.3-70B and GPT-OSS-120B 13.0 / 14.6 (table partly garbled), Llama-3.1-8B 12 to 14. MAE about 0.93 to 1.04. F1 on category 1 (not novel) = 0.0 for every model.
quote: alignment does not reliably translate into accurate novelty judgments
limits: Single venue (ML), gold labels come from reviewer text and are themselves subjective. F1 table text is garbled in extraction; GPT-5 17.2 and o3 16.2 are stated in the text.
agent_relevance: An LLM cannot be trusted as a numeric novelty judge. Its reasoning looks good while its verdict is off. Do not let a self-assigned novelty score gate decisions.

source: Schopf T. & Faerber M. (2026) RINoBench (bias and reasoning effect)
finding: Models avoid extremes. They never call an idea 'not novel' correctly and mostly predict 3 or 4. Reasoning models beat non-reasoning ones by a small margin. Justifications are longer than human ones and rarely hallucinate.
numbers: Hallucination rate of known-aspect arguments 0.0 to 4.2%. Additional-argument ratio often above 100%. Reasoning models only slightly higher F1 than Llama models.
limits: Judge for the justification metrics was GPT-4.1. Small F1 gap between model groups.
agent_relevance: Expect a positive bias toward 'some novelty'. Add an explicit step that argues for 'already known' and counts it, to counter leniency.

source: Si C., Yang D., Hashimoto T. (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review found LLM-agent ideas more novel than expert-written ideas, with other scores about equal. Result holds under three statistical tests.
numbers: 49 ideas per condition (Human, AI, AI + Human Rerank). Per review: novelty Human 4.84 (SD 1.79), AI 5.64 (1.76), AI+rerank 5.81 (1.66); p<0.01. Per idea (N=49): 4.86, 5.62, 5.78; p<0.05. 79 reviewers, 32 institutions.
limits: NLP prompting topics only; ideas not executed; ideas style-normalised; novelty judged by reviewers without running the idea.
agent_relevance: LLM agents can produce ideas that read as novel to experts, so the problem is not generating but filtering and checking.

source: Si C. et al. (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? (LLM judges and diversity)
finding: LLM evaluators agree with experts less than experts agree with each other. The agent also fails to produce diverse ideas at scale.
numbers: Inter-reviewer consistency 56.1%. Best LLM judge (Claude-3.5 pairwise) 53.3%; other judges including AI Scientist reviewer scored lower (about 43 to 52%). Out of 4,000 generated seed ideas only 200 are non-duplicate (about 5%) at cosine similarity threshold 0.8.
limits: Balanced idea-ranking task with median-threshold accuracy; small human set.
agent_relevance: Over-generate and rank hits a ceiling because samples collapse into duplicates; keep a dedup step and use external checks, not self-judging.

source: Si C., Hashimoto T., Yang D. (2025) The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
finding: 43 experts executed randomly assigned ideas from the earlier study. After execution, LLM ideas lost most of their novelty advantage; some metrics flip in favour of human ideas.
numbers: N=43 executors (19 human-idea, 24 AI-idea), 58 reviewers. Novelty change after execution: human -0.010, AI -1.049 on 1-10 scale; excitement +0.078 vs -1.760; effectiveness -0.052 vs -1.879. Gap difference for novelty 1.039 (FDR p=0.025); all four metrics p<0.05.
limits: 43 projects, NLP prompting tasks, execution capped by time, ideas from one agent pipeline.
agent_relevance: Perceived novelty at idea stage is a poor guide to final value. Novelty checks should be repeated after a concrete attempt, not only at proposal time.

source: Gupta T. & Pruthi D. (2025) All That Glitters is Not Novel: Plagiarism in AI Generated Research
finding: 13 experts hunting for overlap found that a quarter of LLM-agent research documents were paraphrased or heavily borrowed from existing work, even though earlier studies rated similar outputs novel.
numbers: 50 documents. 14.0% (7/50) scored 5 (one-to-one methodological mapping) and 10.0% (5/50) scored 4; total 24.0% plagiarism, 36.0% if the milder category is added. Detection accuracy of plagiarism checkers: GPT-4o SSAG 68.5%, Claude SSAG 51.3%, OpenScholar 0%.
limits: Small sample; convenience sampling of experts; a few agent systems; cross-verified by source authors in reported cases.
agent_relevance: The reviewer's frame matters: asking 'find the source' gives very different novelty results than asking 'rate novelty'. Build the search-for-source step into the loop.

source: Beel J. et al. (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist for Autonomous Research
finding: The AI Scientist's novelty check is an LLM plus Semantic Scholar keyword search. It labelled all generated ideas novel, including well-known techniques.
numbers: Up to 10 search results per query, up to 10 iterations. All 10 generated ideas and 2 seed ideas were marked novel, e.g. micro-batching for SGD, adaptive learning rate, hybrid matrix factorization. 42% of experiments failed with coding errors.
limits: Small case study (one domain, recommender systems, laptop run); the AI Scientist can sometimes flag ideas non-novel.
agent_relevance: Keyword literature search plus self-judgment gives false novelty. Check needs concept-level retrieval and an adversarial 'it already exists' pass.

source: Shahid S., Radensky M., Fok R., Siangliulue P., Weld D., Hope T. (2025) Literature-Grounded Novelty Assessment of Scientific Ideas
finding: An LLM retrieve-then-rerank novelty checker with expert-labelled examples beats zero-shot and prompt optimisers. Facet-based reranking of retrieved papers matters most for catching non-novel ideas.
numbers: Accuracy / F1: zero-shot 0.68 / 0.65; DSPy 0.66 to 0.68; TextGrad 0.78 / 0.76; Open-Review in-context 0.59 / 0.43; expert-labelled in-context (idea, papers, class, reasoning) 0.81 / 0.79, kappa 0.59; other novelty checkers 0.47 / 0.44, kappa 0.05.
limits: Small expert-labelled test set (around 60 ideas, inferred from percentages); GPT-4o used Aug-Sep 2024; domain AI/NLP.
agent_relevance: Few-shot examples with expert reasoning move accuracy from 0.68 to 0.81. A reusable pattern: facet extraction, retrieval, rerank, compare.

source: Shahid S. et al. (2025) Literature-Grounded Novelty Assessment (ablation)
finding: Removing pipeline stages collapses the accuracy on 'not novel' ideas. Prompt wording alone also swings accuracy a lot during optimisation.
numbers: Accuracy on 'not novel': complete system 89.66%; without facet reranking (relevance RankGPT) 13.79%; without embedding filtering 10.34%; snippet retrieval only 8.62%; keyword retrieval only 5.17%. Two prompts with different instructions scored 0 and 0.6 accuracy.
limits: Class-specific accuracy on a small set; the ablation uses same data used to design the system.
agent_relevance: Good retrieval is the part that detects 'already exists'. Weak search makes almost every idea look new.

source: Wang Q., Downey D., Ji H., Hope T. (2024) SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
finding: An early loop that retrieves inspirations, generates an idea, compares to prior work, and rewrites until it is not too similar. GPT-4 ideas without this have low novelty and technical depth.
numbers: Iterative novelty boosting: 1st iteration made +54.4%, +55.6%, +47.8%, +46.7% of ideas more novel (four variants); 2nd iteration +57.8% for ideas that continued. Ground-truth paper idea was judged more technically deep and novel in 85% of comparisons vs generated ideas. GPT4FS+KG less incremental in 45% of pairs.
limits: Similarity-to-prior-work threshold as proxy for novelty; added terms often generic ('novel model/method'); annotated subset (about 50 instances).
agent_relevance: The earliest in-loop novelty step: measure similarity to retrieved prior work, then rewrite away from it. Watch for generic padding that looks new but is not.

source: Li L. et al. (2024) Chain of Ideas: Revolutionizing Research Ideation via an LLM Agent
finding: Agent arranges literature as a chain of progressing ideas, to let the LLM see where the field is heading, and is judged by an Idea Arena pairwise protocol.
numbers: Reported quality comparable to human ideas; minimum cost $0.50 per idea. Detailed win rates not extracted.
limits: Only abstract and setup read; Idea Arena uses LLM judges, which c08 and c11 show are unreliable on novelty.
agent_relevance: Ordering references by time gives a trend the model can extrapolate; a cheap context-building move.

source: Hu X. et al. (2024) Nova: An Iterative Planning and Search Approach to Enhance Novelty and Diversity of LLM Generated Ideas
finding: Iterative planning of what to retrieve, then idea generation. More rounds of retrieval raise the count of unique novel ideas.
numbers: 170 seed papers; Swiss Tournament score reported; unique novel ideas 3.4 times higher than the baseline without iterative planning.
limits: Judged partly by LLM Swiss tournament; human assessment details not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Planning which knowledge to fetch next is a way to force new combinations, like pulling distant journals into a paper.

source: Doshi A.R. & Hauser O.P. (2024) Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
finding: In a story-writing experiment, access to GenAI ideas made each story rated more novel and useful, but stories became more similar to each other.
numbers: Novelty +6.7% (b=0.259, p=0.001, from Human-only mean 3.85); usefulness +6.4%; 5 AI ideas: novelty +8.1% (b=0.311, p<0.001). Low-DAT writers: +10.7% novelty with 5 AI ideas. Stories 5.2% more similar to the shown AI idea (b=4.29, p<0.001, human-only mean 82.85); more similar to the average story (b=0.871 with 1 idea, 0.718 with 5).
limits: Short stories, online writers and evaluators; similarity from embeddings; not a science setting.
agent_relevance: Gains in each item's novelty can hide a drop in novelty across the whole set. Measure novelty against the agent's own earlier outputs too.

source: Zhang Y. et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Human-Aligned Novelty
finding: Twenty leading models produce far less diversity of distinct answers than human writers. Larger models in a family are often less diverse than smaller ones.
numbers: 20 models; distinct-k counts equivalence classes among k samples; a human baseline from 8 authors. A classifier for equivalence reached 79% accuracy against human labels. In-context regeneration raises diversity.
limits: Measures distributional diversity across samples, not novelty versus the literature.
agent_relevance: Single-sample novelty scores are meaningless when sampling collapses. Prompt for regeneration with the earlier answers in context.

source: Jiang L. et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
finding: Different models give strikingly similar answers to open-ended queries, so repeated use across models does not add independent novelty.
numbers: INFINITY-CHAT: 26K open-ended queries, 31,250 human annotations (25 per example); 42 models. Mean within-prompt similarity 0.821; cross-model pair similarity 71% to 82% (DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82, vs gpt-4o 0.81).
limits: Similarity from embeddings; novelty vs literature not tested.
agent_relevance: Using several models as a panel does not give independent novelty checks. Ask different models for different roles, not the same question.

source: Uzzi B., Mukherjee S., Stringer M., Jones B. (2013) Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact, as described in Liu et al. 2025
finding: The founding measure, quoted in the LLM papers: z-score of each journal pair in a paper's reference list against randomised citation networks; atypical pairs signal novelty.
numbers: Not read from the original; the LLM papers (c06) only use it as a baseline named URPC.
limits: Second-hand description. Original paper was not opened by this agent.
agent_relevance: Gives the idea of scoring a pair against a null model of what is usually combined. An agent can do that with embeddings or co-occurrence counts.

source: Wang et al. (2017); Bornmann et al. (2019); Fontana et al. (2020) as cited in Wang 2024
finding: Wang 2024 lists the main critique of reference-based novelty: coarse knowledge units, citations made for non-intellectual reasons, and conflation with interdisciplinarity (Fontana 2020). Bornmann 2019 is a validation of unusual-combination indicators on F1000Prime data.
numbers: No numbers read from the originals.
limits: Only citations seen in c01; originals not opened.
agent_relevance: Reminder that atypicality and novelty are different; an agent should keep 'distant' and 'new' as separate flags.

source: Lu C. et al. (2024) The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery, as analysed in Beel 2025
finding: An agent loop that generates ideas, then checks novelty by querying Semantic Scholar before running experiments. This is a method from this subfield (prior-work comparison) used inside a real agent loop.
numbers: Loop details taken from c14: up to 10 results per query, up to 10 query rounds, binary novel label. Original PDF downloaded but only title read.
limits: Description is second-hand from c14. Original not read in depth.
agent_relevance: Shows the minimal form of an in-loop novelty gate and how it fails (c14).

source: Park M., Leahey E., Funk R. (2023) Papers and patents are becoming less disruptive over time, as cited in Liu 2025 and Safari 2026
finding: Cited by the LLM-novelty papers as the motivation: published papers and patents show a decline in novelty and disruption despite growth in output.
numbers: No figures read here.
limits: Second-hand citation only.
agent_relevance: Sets the stakes: novelty measures exist because volume grows while disruption falls; an LLM agent adding volume could worsen it.

source: Kobak D. et al. (2025) and Kwon & Yang (2025) as cited in Safari & Babaei 2026
finding: Reported by Safari: detectable LLM-related vocabulary differs widely by country, field and journal; CS paper output rose after ChatGPT.
numbers: Kwon and Yang: more than 218,000 CS papers (as reported).
limits: Second-hand, originals not opened.
agent_relevance: Surface vocabulary shifts in text are a trap for text-based novelty scores.

source: Schopf & Faerber (2026) RINoBench related-work summary of automated novelty methods
finding: Lists the progression: atypical cited-reference combinations (Uzzi 2013), journal-vector cosine (Wang 2017), lexical similarity, then embeddings, then retrieval-augmented LLMs. Notes LLM approaches often give only binary labels, ground rationales poorly, and call well-known ideas novel.
numbers: Only publicly available prior evaluation dataset (Shahid et al. 2025) had 51 labelled items (as stated in the paper).
limits: Survey sentence in a benchmark paper; not exhaustive.
agent_relevance: Gives the lineage from citation-pair scores to LLM judges, and the known failure: unseen paraphrases pass as new.
